title: AI-Infused Collaborative Inquiry in Upper Elementary School: A Game-Based Learning Approach
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge of introducing AI learning experiences into K-12 education, with a particular focus on the elementary grades where there is very limited prior work. The authors ask how to create engaging upper-elementary learning experiences that integrate AI and life science, and how to support teachers in bringing these experiences into their classrooms.

The intervention/approach is PRIMARYAI, a game-based learning environment designed for upper elementary students. It combines inquiry-based science, problem-based learning, and block-based programming so students can learn AI concepts such as classification, machine learning, perception, and semi-autonomous navigation while solving an ecology problem about declining yellow-eyed penguin populations. The game is designed for collaborative small-group work in class and is grounded in NGSS and the K-12 Computer Science Framework.

The paper also reports a co-design component with three elementary STEM coaches in the Midwestern United States. The teachers participated in semi-structured interviews about their experience, confidence, and support needs related to computer science and AI. The qualitative findings suggest that teachers see AI as important but need substantial professional development, especially around AI content knowledge, plus grade-level-appropriate materials and follow-up classroom support. The paper concludes that combining AI-infused game-based learning with teacher support may be a promising way to introduce AI into upper elementary classrooms, but the system remains in development and needs classroom evaluation.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed design/research paper with a small qualitative component (n=3 teacher interviews) and no completed student efficacy evaluation. Methodologically it is useful for understanding implementation and design, but it does not meet RCT/QED standards for impact evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports no measured student impacts yet; its contributions are design-oriented and implementation-focused. Any likely impact is still speculative because the classroom studies and pre/post assessments are only planned.

interventions.use_case: Game-based collaborative inquiry environment (PRIMARYAI) for upper elementary students to learn AI concepts through life-science problem solving, including block-based programming of semi-autonomous robots and classifier-building tasks.

finding.finding_summary: This paper does not report a completed efficacy result for student science learning; instead, it presents the design of PRIMARYAI and plans future pre/post classroom studies to measure AI and life-science learning. The authors state that the environment is intended to support inquiry-based problem solving in ecology/life science, but no effect sizes or outcome data are reported.
finding.measure: Planned pre/post assessments of AI concepts, AI ethics, and life science concepts

finding.finding_summary: No quantitative engagement results are reported, but the paper explicitly proposes measuring behavioral, social, and emotional engagement in future classroom studies of PRIMARYAI. The qualitative teacher interviews suggest the design is intended to be engaging, but evidence is prospective rather than outcome-based.
finding.measure: Planned engagement coding of group work (behavioral, social, emotional engagement)
finding.study_size: n=3 teachers for qualitative needs analysis; student engagement data not yet collected

finding.finding_summary: The paper frames PRIMARYAI as supporting collaboration, problem solving, and hypothesis discussion during group inquiry, but it does not provide student outcome data. The only empirical component is a small qualitative teacher interview study (n=3) indicating that teachers want grade-appropriate, open-ended curricula and professional development to support implementation.
finding.measure: Qualitative interview themes on pedagogical support needs and collaborative inquiry design

finding.finding_summary: The teacher interview findings indicate strong perceived need for AI professional development, curriculum support, and follow-up classroom coaching to enable adoption of AI-infused inquiry lessons in elementary classrooms. This is a qualitative implementation finding rather than a student outcome, with no effect size reported.
finding.measure: Semi-structured teacher interviews on implementation supports and readiness
